subtopics.title: Recognising a Cube When You See One

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY perfect cubes?
In $x^3 + 8$ written as $a^3 + b^3$, the values of a and b are:
Why can't $x^3 + 8$ be factorised with the difference-of-squares or trinomial methods?
options: It can — squares work fine on it
It is a SUM of two terms that are cubes, not squares, and has no middle term — only the cubes identity fits

questions.question: Which of these is also a perfect cube?

subtopics.title: The Identity and the SOAP Mnemonic

questions.question: In the SOAP mnemonic, the letters stand for:
options: Same, Opposite, Always Positive — the three signs of the factorisation

questions.question: The second bracket of a cubes factorisation is built by:
options: Square the first, square the last, halve the middle
Square the first, multiply the pair, square the last

questions.question: When $(a + b)(a^2 - ab + b^2)$ is expanded, what happens to the middle terms?
options: $-a^2b$ cancels $+a^2b$ and $+ab^2$ cancels $-ab^2$, leaving only $a^3 + b^3$
Nothing cancels — all six terms remain

questions.question: $x^3 + 8$ factorises as:
A learner writes the middle term of the second bracket as $-4x$. The error is:
options: The middle term is $a \times b = 2x$ — the learner squared the 2 instead of multiplying

questions.question: Why does $x^2 - 2x + 4$ stay unfactorised in the final answer?
options: The exam does not require it
No number pair has product 4 and sum −2 — the quadratic factor of a cubes identity never factorises over the real numbers
It cancels with the first bracket

subtopics.title: The Difference Twin and the Full Method

questions.question: $x^3 - 27$ factorises as:
To factorise $2x^3 - 54$ fully, the first move is:
options: Take out the common factor 2, revealing $2(x^3 - 27)$, then apply the cubes identity

questions.question: How do the factorisations of $x^2 - 9$ (squares) and $x^3 - 27$ (cubes) differ in shape?
options: Squares give two linear brackets; cubes give one linear and one quadratic bracket that stays

questions.question: Which check should end every cubes factorisation?
options: Expand and watch the middle terms cancel back to the original two terms
Compare with the difference of squares
No check is needed for identities

subtopics.title: Cubes Are Just Boxes You Can Stack

questions.question: Which number is NOT on the lesson's list of six perfect cubes?
Why is $y^6$ a perfect cube?
options: Because $y^2$ stacked three times gives $y^6$ — the block being cubed is $y^2$
Because every power of y is a cube

questions.question: Two terms, a plus sign between them, no common factor and no squares in sight. What is the signal?
options: Use the difference of squares anyway
Check whether each term is something cubed — this is the cubes identity's territory

questions.question: In $x^3 + 8$, the 'two names' you carry into the answer are:

subtopics.title: Three Signs, One Bar of Soap

questions.question: The three pieces of the LONG bracket are built by:
options: Square the first name, multiply the two names, square the last name
Adding the two names three times

questions.question: SOAP stands for the three signs:
When $(x + 2)$ and $(x^2 - 2x + 4)$ are multiplied out, why is only $x^3 + 8$ left?
options: The four middle products cancel in pairs — $-2x^2$ against $+2x^2$, and $+4x$ against $-4x$
The middle terms are simply ignored
Because x is assumed to be 0

questions.question: A learner writes the long bracket as $x^2 - 4x + 4$. What went wrong?
options: The middle should be the two names MULTIPLIED ($2x$); the learner squared the 2 instead

subtopics.title: The Curtain, the Twin and Knowing When to Stop

questions.question: Running SOAP on $x^3 - 27$ gives:
'Taking the wrapper off' $2x^3 - 54$ means:
options: Taking out the common factor 2 to reveal $2(x^3 - 27)$

questions.question: Why do you leave $x^2 + 3x + 9$ exactly as it is?
options: Because the exam runs out of space
Because it cancels with the short bracket
Because no number pair multiplies to 9 and adds to 3 — the long bracket never breaks at this level

questions.question: Which check tells you to use squares rather than cubes?
options: The exponent: 'squared' calls the squares method, 'cubed' calls the cubes method
The size of the numbers involved
Whether the sign is plus or minus
Whether the expression contains an x
